subject: giraffe
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module that constructs a stylized giraffe using the SDK's builder API—setting up joints, chains, and parts for a rigged skeleton with patch paints, keeping it compact but using the APIs correctly.

Now I'm working out realistic proportions: hooves at ground level, chest height around 2.2m, shoulder line near 2.3m, and head top around 5.2m, with the long neck and legs scaled accordingly. I'm deciding to build the body as a loft along the z-axis from rump to chest, defining stations with width and height to shape the torso.

For the neck, I'll use a chain of joints following a curved path with a sweep radius that tapers from thick at the base to narrower at the top. The head gets its own joint with a jaw sub-joint and simple box/capsule shapes, plus rod-shaped ossicones colored dark brown, and I'm now planning the four legs.

For legs, I'm working out how to build each one as a chain of joints (hip, knee, ankle, hoof) along a polyline path, figuring out how many spans and names are needed so each joint lands at the right point like hip, knee, and ankle, with the hoof as the tip joint.

I decide to pass the parent explicitly as "torso" since the joint positions aren't owned by any mesh and would otherwise fall back to nearest-joint logic. For the leg geometry itself, I'll sweep the chain with a tapering radius function and place small capsules or cylinders at the hooves, then move on to positioning the body and legs symmetrically around the center with the giraffe facing forward.

I'm laying out the torso as a loft between rump, mid, and chest stations at specific widths and heights, then placing hip and shoulder joints with knees, ankles, and hooves following down to ground level for both front and hind legs. I'm making sure the root torso joint gets created before any chains that depend on it as a parent.

Now I'm building the neck as a multi-point chain angling up and forward toward the head, with the final tip joint becoming the head, and I'm planning a sweep profile that tapers the neck radius while applying a patched paint color scheme in ochre and brown. I'm also starting to add a jaw joint as a child of the head.

Setting up the jaw joint hierarchy...

I need the jaw joint to be a child of the head joint, using the role "jaw" with hinge axis along the bone's X, positioned via the head's local frame. I'll attach the jaw part using the joint's frame directly so the geometry offset is relative to that local frame rather than recalculating world coordinates.

For the eyes, I'm placing small black spheres on either side of the head using the head's local frame, working out that local +X corresponds to world -X (the creature's right side) given the head's pitch orientation.

For the ossicones, I'm building each as a rod running from a point near the base of the head up and outward to a tip, dark brown in color, with a small sphere knob capping the tip, making sure to explicitly set the bone to "head" since the rod's endpoints are plain vectors without weight data to infer that automatically.

For ears, I'm keeping things simple with small boxes positioned on either side of the head, framed to the head bone.

For the tail, I'm chaining four joints running from the rump down and back, parented to the torso with a tapering sweep in the body color, and capping the tip with a small sphere tuft attached to the final tail joint.

Now I'm starting on the legs, defining point sets for each of the four and sweeping them with a tapering radius.

Writing leg hierarchy...

For hind legs I'm setting the hock joint further back with hip, knee, ankle, and hoof positions adjusted for the backward bend. I'm using the leg chain's hoof point for contact detection automatically. Now I'm moving on to the body patches, designing irregular brown polygon patches on the ochre base coat to mimic giraffe markings.

Setting up the hooves, muzzle, and mane details, then defining the body loft stations with their width and height profiles for the catmull-rom surface.

For the neck, I'm plotting a curved chain of points from chest to head with increasing height and forward offset, naming the joints neckA through neckC and tip head, then sweeping a tube along that chain with a radius tapering from base to tip.

Now I'm working out the head geometry details -- positioning ossicones relative to the top of the head box, placing eyes on the sides, and figuring out where the jaw joint and jaw box should sit relative to the head's local coordinate space so the mouth hangs correctly below and behind the skull.

Still working out ossicone and eye placement...

Positioning the muzzle box in front of the head, overlapping slightly with the head's lower-front region, and giving it a lighter tan color. For the jaw, I'm sizing and placing a box near the back-bottom of the head to act as the hinge point for the jaw bone.

Now I'm working out the tail: a chain of joints curving backward and downward from the torso, with a tapered rope-like sweep and a small dark tuft sphere at the tip. For the body, I'm defining loft stations along the z-axis—rump, mid-body, and chest—each with its own width and height, checking that the rounded end caps and neck placement overlap correctly with the body's top and front dimensions.

Writing leg joint chains...

I'm sketching out the fore and hind leg joint chains from hip through knee/stifle to ankle and hoof, tapering the sweep radius down each leg, then placing small cylinder geometries as hooves anchored at the ankle-chain endpoints so their bottoms sit flush with the ground.

Writing module imports and setup...

I'm setting up the module with imports from three.js and the agentic-3js-builder, defining a coat color using a patches function with brown/tan blotches for camouflage spots, and establishing the root torso joint with its position and forward-facing direction.

Writing loft and chain code...

I'm defining the body loft from the rump/mid/chest stations, then building the neck as a chain of joints curving upward and forward from the torso, checking that the chain's point count matches its name count, and tapering the neck's sweep radius from base to head.

Writing leg function...

I'm writing a reusable leg-building function that takes a side and prefix, constructs the joint chain, applies the tapered sweep, and attaches a hoof cylinder part anchored at the final chain point, then calling it for each of the four legs with their own hip/knee/ankle/hoof coordinates.

Writing head details...

I'm adding head geometry — a boxy skull, a forward muzzle, a jaw joint with hinge behavior, small eye spheres, ear boxes angled outward, and tail tuft sphere — all anchored to the head joint's local frame so they inherit its position and rotation correctly, then double-checking hoof heights and head height sum to a believable giraffe silhouette before finalizing the module with its meta export.
